title: Commercial Fusion Energy in 2026: Assembly Advances, Funding Decides Pace

stats.label: Fusion funding raised in 12 months
stats.detail: Record worldwide total in the 12 months to July 2026, mostly private investors (Fusion Industry Association, via Reuters).

stats.label: Cumulative funding since 2021
stats.detail: Total cumulative funding reported by the Fusion Industry Association since 2021.

stats.label: ITER sector modules installed
stats.detail: Sixth module lowered in a 30-hour lift on 28 July 2026, nearly six months ahead of schedule; two-thirds of the tokamak core now in place.

stats.label: U.S. target for fusion deployment
stats.detail: DOE Fusion Science and Technology Roadmap, released June 2026, sets the federal strategy's deployment goal.

stats.label: U.S. fusion companies building devices
stats.detail: Most pursue tokamaks or stellarators; others use laser-based inertial confinement (Fusion Industry Association, 2026).

stats.label: FY2027 fusion energy sciences funding
stats.detail: Appropriated below the $805.7 million enacted and far under the $1.1 billion authorized for FES in 2022 legislation.

quotes.text: "The plan isn't the problem. We all agree on the plan. The X factor is the funding. If we underfund the U.S. fusion program... we can all watch the timeline to commercialisation slip."
quotes.source: Robb Hughes, Realta Fusion, via Reuters

quotes.text: Private developers have not yet achieved "net energy gain," the point where a fusion reaction produces more energy than was used to start and sustain it.
quotes.source: Reuters, US roadmap targets fusion deployment by mid 2030s

quotes.text: "With six modules now in place, we are demonstrating that this technical approach is delivering tangible results on the project's critical path."
Fusion fuel is extremely energy-dense, but tritium is scarce on Earth and decays with a half-life of about 12.3 years.

takeaway: Fusion's binding constraints in 2026 are tritium, neutron-resistant materials and appropriations — not the physics.
